implementation: src/codepilot/llm/openai_compatible.py: _send_before_deadline streams the response and checks time.monotonic() against one request-total deadline after every chunk; exceeding it raises httpx.ReadTimeout('请求总时限 %ss 已耗尽：持续响应超过 deadline').
The response is rebuilt from buffered chunks only after the full body arrives; leaving the context closes that response without closing the shared httpx client.

src/codepilot/llm/retry.py: call_with_retry invokes a before_retry callback after on_retry and before sleeping; openai_compatible.complete passes lambda: check_dispatch('model') so a post-timeout re-dispatch cannot overwrite the unknown-billing outcome.
Per-phase connect/read/write/pool timeouts remain; they are no longer treated as a request total.
http_total_deadline.evidence: loopback-only fake HTTP servers; no provider request. Admission outcomes observed: settled with trusted usage, unknown+frozen after dispatch timeout, cancelled+refund before HTTP.

decisions: Node bodies stay synchronous I/O inside a private loop per node, executed via asyncio.to_thread; the task-level asyncio loop owns graph/checkpoint orchestration only.

src/codepilot/observability/events.py: EventSink uses threading.RLock around the whole emit path so seq allocation, JSONL append, API mirror and runtime projection stay atomic; close() and last_seq also take the lock.
src/codepilot/graph/checkpoint.py: open_checkpointer awaits aiosqlite.connect; without the await, __aexit__ raised ValueError('no active connection') and masked CheckpointIdentityError.
SQLAlchemy sessions are never used concurrently: one task graph executes nodes sequentially and each node completes before the next starts; no pool sharing across tasks.
No async object bound to the task loop is reused inside a node loop; the shared httpx client is synchronous and only reached through its thread-safe connection pool.

contextvars, dispatch deadline, cancellation event and source attribution are established at the node boundary; asyncio.shield keeps node result delivery, and CancelledError waits for the worker thread instead of abandoning live side effects.
ownership.tests: tests/graph/test_phase26_ownership.py: 5 passed; tests/graph/test_resume.py: 16 passed; batch suite: 46 passed
ownership.evidence: cancel observed CANCELLED + StopReason.CANCELLED with usage.llm_calls retained; checkpoint state read back as CANCELLED; resume_run did not replay a completed fake call; no leaked threads after cancellation.

implementation: src/codepilot/graph/validation_time.py: estimate_timeout only considers samples whose candidate identity matches; historical 250s / suggested 320s / runner cap 300s no longer refuses dispatch for insufficient margin.

src/codepilot/graph/deps.py AccountingSandbox.run_tests: resource slot -> identity -> estimate -> final_timeout = dispatch_timeout(min(env.timeout_seconds, suggested)) -> check_dispatch('test') -> runs += 1 -> inner run -> timing facts. Remaining deadline is rechecked after the slot is acquired; a run stopped before dispatch neither counts nor records.
Closure reservation is deducted once from the remaining window; aggregate/file-level evidence never promotes an incomplete scope to complete.
estimation_and_recovery.recovery: checkpoint after cancel is readable and resume continues from the valid checkpoint; completed fake calls are not replayed; official-only recovery uses a fake runner and does not call internal inference; invalid results remain recoverable and ledger/history is not rewritten.
